Egham Park will offer blended learning in that all the programmes of study can be accessed online, and through workbooks and worksheets.

Ofsted Report: A Letter To Parents
Dear Parents and Guardians,
I am delighted to be able to tell you we have now received our final Ofsted Report, which will be available on the school website shortly.
I am so proud to share with you that after being open for just 10 months we have received a wonderful rating of ‘Good’ in all areas.
This accomplishment reflects the dedication and hard work of our students and staff. It is a testament to the positive and nurturing learning environment that we strive to create at Egham Park.
The report states that “Pupil’s experiences at this inclusive, happy school give them a hope for a different future”, as well as “From the moments they walk through the doors, pupils know that their academic journey will never be overwhelming here.” Please do read the full report.
We appreciate the ongoing support and collaboration between school and our families. Together we can continue to create a school environment that empowers out students and prepares them for their ‘next steps.’
Thank you for being an integral part of the Egham Park community. I cannot express how very proud I am of how much we have achieved in such a short time.
If you have any questions or would like further details about the Ofsted Report, please do not hesitate to ask.

Nature and Nurture
At Egham Park School, supporting pupils’ emotional wellbeing, engagement, and sense of belonging is at the heart of everything we do.
Our school allotment provides learners with regular hands-on opportunities to develop responsibility, patience, teamwork, and practical life skills in a calm and purposeful environment where they can experience success and build confidence.
Environmental Learning to All
We are proud to actively promote environmental learning across the school through initiatives such as the Woodland Trust Green Tree Schools Award, and the RHS School Gardening Awards
These programmes help us embed nature-based learning throughout the curriculum while encouraging pupils to take ownership of their environment and develop a sense of achievement.
By continuing to enhance biodiversity within our school grounds and expand opportunities for outdoor learning, we aim to create a safe, nurturing environment where all learners can thrive while developing respect for the natural world alongside improved wellbeing and valuable life skills.

About Egham Park
A small specialist independent provision offering an alternative educational experience
The pupils who will attend Egham Park will be placed at the school by the Local Education Authority. Their primary area of need will be Social, Emotional and Mental Health Needs (SEMH).
Most will come to us having had previous negative experience of school, resulting in emotional based school avoidance for many. As a result, many will have been out of school for some time, and many will join us late in their secondary educational career.
The school offers a very flexible, low demand, low arousal environment where pupils are at the centre of their learning choices. This will equip them to feel empowered and safe within the environment.
Each pupil will have a bespoke differentiated curriculum. Whilst they will follow a timetable of subjects, they will be able to make choices as to what they are studying under those subject headings, thus motivating them to engage in learning.
Egham Park offers a variety of learning experiences in that the programmes of study can be accessed online, and through workbooks and worksheets. This means that pupils can access their learning within the school environment, or from home, dependent upon their individual circumstances at the time. This then enables pupils to follow a bespoke, differentiated curriculum that is pupil led, motivating and accessible from school and home.
Egham Park School has two sites within a short walk of each other,
At our High Street site is based over three floors and hosts Magna Carta and Runnymede classes. There is a maximum of 45 pupils throughout the school. Students will access their individual learning programme at their own pace whilst being supported by the teachers and support staff.
Holloway class is based at our Waspe Farm site, which has two classrooms and outside space. This setting accommodates a maximum of 10 pupils who benefit from a smaller environment and the opportunity to develop safe and secure relationships with trusted adults. At both sites staff work closely with pupils to develop their social, emotional and mental health through a nurturing approach which is embedded in the PACE approach and supported by a range of evidence informed practice such as ELSA, Mentoring and Speech and Language support.
In Holloway class, the curriculum is personalised and based around the individual needs and interests of each pupil. We focus on embedding key skills in Maths and English and incorporate a wide range of practical lessons throughout the week, such as Arts, STEM, Gardening, Physical Welling, PSHE and Social Skills.
Over both sites pupils can engage in units and courses that result in a qualification, units and courses that result in a Certificate of Achievement or a combination of both. This will be determined by the students, interests, abilities and time of joining us. The learning journey decided upon is also fluid, dependent upon individual circumstances at any given time.
Our aim for all pupils is that they experience a positive association with education and learning, thus preparing them for the step of their own journey. This may be taking their first qualifications at college, further qualifications at college, employment or an apprenticeship.
135-139 High Street, Egham, Surrey, TW20 9HL

The young persons Education Health Care Planis sent to us from the Local Authority for consideration.
The paperwork is carefully perused to establish whether Egham Park would be an appropriate placement for the young person.
We will then invite the potential pupil and their parent/carer to visit the school and to meet the principal. It is during this time that all parties can consider whether the placement is likely to work. After the visit everyone can take a little time to reflect upon the appropriateness of the potential placement.
If all agree, then the young person will be invited for a taster or a series of taster sessions so that all involved can gain a better understanding of whether Egham Park is an appropriate placement.
If this is successful, we advise the local authority that we can offer a placement, and they will then put the proposal to panel to see if they will agree to fund the placement.
If approved, we will then arrange for a start date for the young person.
It is highly likely that many of our pupils will require a step-by-step transition plan to help them adjust to school and we create this based upon their individual needs. It is adjusted as time goes on because some young people adjust and settle quicker or slower than they originally anticipated.
Some young people many need to take a step back and restart their learning from an earlier point. We work collaboratively with everyone with everyone involved to ensure we establish the right ‘level’ for the individual. An example of this is where a young person is so anxious that the priority is to get them into school. Only when they are attending more regularly can we assess their level of learning and the best ‘starting point’ for them as an individual
Once the start date has been determined, if applicable the parents/carers will need to arrange transport with the Local Authority. This can take some time
We will request the young person's files from their previous setting and ask that parents/carers complete and respond all forms provided to them from Egham Park as quickly as possible
In collaboration with the young person, parent/carer, and relevant professionals, we will work in a bespoke integration plan for the young person to ensures that their start at Egham Park is as stress free and successful as possible. This will include baseline academic testing.
